feedback: Approve for this race. The candidate changes one controller value from the best raced design (iteration 4, score 313.7): kd goes from 0.45 to 0.60, with kp 2.6, ki 0.1, base_speed 1.2, the ±0.07 m five-sensor span, sensor_size 0.016 and the weights held fixed. This is the rule I set after iteration 4. Its evidence: steering_oscillation was 0.286 on the oval and 0.213 on the s-bend, both above the 0.2 level, and iteration 4 gave 13 of 20 oval finishes but 0 on the s-bend and slalom. Line_loss_events fell to 0.15 on the oval and 0.0 on the s-bend and slalom, so the widened span is working and the remaining problem is steering behaviour and off-track endings. The candidate is valid: all sensor positions are inside the allowed ranges, sensor_size 0.016 is an allowed option, and the weights, line_loss and observation list are allowed. Nothing in it is obviously broken. The main risk is that more kd amplifies sensor noise and raises oscillation on the slalom, and that the s-bend max_error stays near 0.06. I cannot say how it will perform. With six iterations left, racing this single-variable step gives clearer telemetry than another reading-only round. Next race, read the results as follows. If steering_oscillation falls below 0.2 on the oval and s-bend and max_error on the s-bend is under 0.06, keep kd near 0.6 and raise base_speed in 0.1 steps (1.3, then 1.4) to test completion_time under 3 s. If oscillation is still above 0.2 at kd 0.6, change the sensor geometry (y position or sensor_size 0.012) before adding more damping. If slalom oscillation rises sharply, the extra kd is amplifying noise, so return kd to about 0.5.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation is still above 0.2 on the oval or s-bend at kd 0.6 with kp 2.6, do not raise kd further. Test sensor y position (for example y at 0.03 m) or sensor_size 0.012 for the off-track endings (iteration 4 gave oscillation of 0.286 on the oval and 0.213 on the s-bend at kd 0.45).

If the run is clean (steering_oscillation under 0.2, line_loss_events near 0, max_error under 0.06 on the s-bend), raise base_speed in 0.1 steps to 1.3, then 1.4, keeping kp 2.6 and kd 0.6 fixed, to test completion_time under 3 s (iteration 1 reached progress 0.37 on the oval at base_speed 1.4).
If slalom steering_oscillation rises well above its iteration 4 level of 0.102 at kd 0.6, the extra damping is amplifying sensor noise. Return kd to about 0.5 and keep kp at 2.6.
